subject: Payment treatment and tax-id aggregation for multi-entity remits (Praxis Health)
messages:
From: Jamie Ortiz <jamie.ortiz@praxishealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Accounting Ops <acctops@praxishealth.com>
Date: 2026-09-14T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Need multi-entity invoice setup + aggregated tax IDs for remits

Jonas —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We’re moving to procurement and need to understand how Redwood will deliver invoices and remittance detail. Praxis has three legal entities that need to appear on billing records and in some cases require separate invoices to route to different AP teams. A few specifics: 

- Some cost centers want line-level cost-center codes (e.g., CC-1203 / CC-1302) on the invoice.
- Our treasury team asks that tax/VAT identifiers for each legal entity are included on the remittance advice so our bank reconciliation can apply payments correctly.
- Preferred outcome: single consolidated PDF for our records + CSV ledger per legal entity for upload into our AR system, OR separate invoices per legal entity depending on Redwood’s capability.

I attached the PO and an initial mapping file (praxis_entity_mapping.xlsx) showing where flows need to land. Can you confirm what you can support and the typical timeline for a new mapping? Also note two cost centers require Net45 terms, the rest Net30.

Thanks,
Jamie Ortiz
Director, Procurement
Praxis Health

Attachments: praxis_po_5842.pdf, praxis_entity_mapping.xlsx

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Jamie Ortiz <jamie.ortiz@praxishealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-14T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Need multi-entity invoice setup + aggregated tax IDs for remits

Jamie —

Appreciate the PO and mapping file. We can support both approaches you listed but there are trade-offs to be explicit about:

Option A (recommended for month-end reconciliation): single consolidated invoice PDF + per-entity CSV/ledger exports. Pros: one invoice number for the account, easier consolidated reporting; Cons: your AR teams will need the CSV to post by legal entity.

Option B: separate invoices per legal entity. Pros: native posting per ledgers in legacy ERPs; Cons: requires unique invoice numbering per entity and slightly more work in our billing pipeline (we can automate it).

Questions for your team so we can scope implementation:
- Do you require distinct invoice numbers per legal entity? (sounds like yes for two entities)
- Do you need the tax/VAT identifier printed on every invoice line or is a remittance summary with all entity tax IDs sufficient?
- For entities that require Net45, is there a specific cost-center-level flag in your mapping spreadsheet?

Technical notes: we will need a final mapping table (entity, legal_name, tax_id, remit_bank, remit_email, payment_terms, cost_center_code) and a contact at your AP team for validation. If we proceed this week, we can target a staged rollout before your next billing cycle (approx. 10 business days).

I’m looping in Kimberly and Laura from finance to confirm the ledger exports and numbering constraints. I can schedule a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk through the mapping.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Head of Customer Billing — Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com

Attachments: none

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Jamie Ortiz <jamie.ortiz@praxishealth.com>
Date: 2026-09-14T15:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Need multi-entity invoice setup + aggregated tax IDs for remits

Jamie / team —

Quick technical summary from Redwood finance/ops on constraints and recommended implementation pattern: 

1) Invoice numbers: Our billing engine can emit either (a) a single master invoice number with line-level entity tags, or (b) one invoice per legal entity with unique invoice numbers. If Praxis requires legal-entity-level audit trails in your GL, choose (b).

2) Remittance / Tax IDs: We can include tax/VAT identifiers three ways: printed on every invoice header, included in a consolidated remittance PDF, or appended as a top-level CSV column used by your bank reconciliation. For your stated need (bank reconciliation by tax id), we recommend a consolidated remittance summary that lists each legal entity and tax id, plus entity-specific CSVs for automated upload.

3) Cost-center line items: We will map cost_center_code to invoice lines (description + custom fields). Please confirm whether cost_center_code must appear in a dedicated CSV field or embedded in the line description for your ERP parser.

4) Payment terms: Our system supports mixed payment terms across lines only when invoices are split per-entity. If you must honor Net45 for specific cost centers while others are Net30, we recommend separate invoices for those entities.

Next steps we need from Praxis before we proceed:
- Finalized mapping spreadsheet with the columns I listed.
- Legal-tax IDs (ideally in CSV).
- AP test contact for one sample invoice validation (email + preferred file format).

I’ll prepare a sample output set (consolidated PDF + per-entity CSV + ledger CSV) based on your sample mapping and send it for validation. Target: sample package 48 hours after we receive the finalized mapping.

Cheers,
Kimberly Park
Senior Manager, Billing Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments (to be sent with sample): entity_tax_ids.csv, sample_consolidated_remit.pdf
